comment: No EU/EEA member state with a federated, market-based delivery system appears among the examples, and the Netherlands is absent altogether. It is an unusually informative case because it separates technical maturity from ordering capacity: high digitisation, mature standards, twenty years of national programmes, and persistent discontinuity of information between providers.

public.text: No EU/EEA member state with a federated, market-based delivery system appears among the examples, and the Netherlands is absent altogether. It is an unusually informative case because it separates technical maturity from ordering capacity: high digitisation, mature standards, twenty years of national programmes, and persistent discontinuity of information between providers.
public.suggestedRevision: Add the Netherlands with two documented episodes. First, a national exchange infrastructure technically completed while its enabling legislation was rejected by the Senate in 2011, after which it continued on a private-law basis with voluntary participation - a direct illustration of the legal dimension identified in 4.6.2 as deserving equal weight. Second, the personal health environment programme, in which a subsidised market of applications was created without any party made responsible for the underlying function, so that when the subsidy ended a statutory right of access became unexercisable. Both are matters of public record.
